scope: Primary-source research for legal/privacy/crypto policy context. No repository edits or claims of exhaustive jurisdiction coverage.

items.title: Brazil adds reporting for larger self-custody transfers
items.summary: BCB-regulated institutions must report virtual-asset transfers of at least US$10,000 equivalent to or from self-custodied wallets to Coaf. The amendment took effect on 1 October 2026.
items.scopeNote: Applies to institutions authorized to operate by BCB under Circular 3978/2020. Do not turn this reporting obligation into a general ban on self-custody, or a duty imposed directly on every private wallet owner.
items.dateNote: Instrument dated 23 September; official publication 25 September, DOU section 1, page 84. BCB press note appeared 23 September; Coaf operational notice appeared 30 September.

supportingSources.supports: Operational Siscoaf implementation from 1 October; occurrence 1676 for self-custody transfers at or above US$10,000 equivalent.
Official explanatory release; date also present as Atom updated 2026-09-23T18:30:57-03:00.

items.title: DeCripto reporting covers transactions from July 2026
items.summary: Receita Federal confirms that transactions from July 2026 move to DeCripto reporting, including covered overseas providers serving Brazil. The reporting duty is separate from whether tax is owed.
items.scopeNote: The source explains IN RFB 2291/2025 and foreign providers directing activities at Brazil under Article 5. Do not infer every holder has identical reporting obligations or state unverified tax thresholds.
items.dateNote: Publication date is the official explanatory article, not the original normative instrument. Application date refers to the transaction period, not an all-user filing deadline.

supportingSources.supports: Official DeCripto hub linking normative instrument and manuals.
Exact normative link found on the official DeCripto hub; JavaScript app not fully extractable in this research.
Official FAQ confirms DeCripto treatment from 1 July 2026.

items.title: Argentina regulates crypto-service providers
items.summary: CNV’s PSAV framework sets registration, custody, cybersecurity and disclosure requirements for covered crypto-service providers. Most requirements for providers already registered became enforceable on 31 December 2025.
items.scopeNote: Service-provider rules, not a finding about Zcash legal status or investment quality. Transitional dates vary by requirement; 31 December concerns Article 7(3) for already registered providers.
items.dateNote: Resolution dated 12 March, Gazette publication 14 March. Current official PSAV registry confirms 26 May 2025 general entry into force. Different transitional deadlines must not be collapsed into one.

supportingSources.supports: Official registry states the 26 May 2025 entry-into-force date.

items.title: EU anonymous-account restriction applies from July 2027
items.summary: From 10 July 2027, Article 79 restricts covered institutions’ anonymous or transaction-obfuscating accounts, including through anonymity-enhancing coins. The regulation does not name Zcash.
items.scopeNote: Article 79 concerns credit institutions, financial institutions and crypto-asset service providers. This is not a general prohibition on holding Zcash or using self-custody. Do not equate a protocol property with a definitive listing determination.
items.dateNote: Article 90 separates entry into force, the twentieth day following publication, from general application on 10 July 2027. In force does not mean Article 79 is already applicable.

items.title: SEC proposes a crypto-custody framework
items.summary: The SEC proposed a crypto-custody framework for registered advisers and regulated funds, including self-custody in specified circumstances. It remains a proposal; comments run 60 days from Federal Register publication.
items.scopeNote: Concerns registered investment advisers and regulated funds; the proposal is not a general self-custody authorization or a rule already in force.
items.dateNote: Do not calculate the comment deadline from 1 October. The release specifies 60 days following Federal Register publication, whose date was not verified.

items.title: FATF reviews virtual-asset implementation gaps
items.summary: FATF’s seventh update calls for stronger virtual-asset standards implementation, including Travel Rule supervision and risks involving unhosted wallets and DeFi. The report is guidance, not directly applicable national law.
items.scopeNote: Intergovernmental standard-setter report. Domestic obligations depend on relevant enacted national rules; FATF recommendations alone do not establish whether an individual wallet or token is prohibited.
items.dateNote: Report publication date only; there is no new directly applicable worldwide effective date.

items.title: Treasury removed Tornado Cash sanctions
items.summary: Treasury removed economic sanctions against Tornado Cash on 21 March 2025. The delisting is a specific administrative action, not a general exemption from sanctions or other financial-crime laws.
items.scopeNote: Historical action concerning Tornado Cash. Do not imply all litigation ended, all privacy software is exempt, or that this establishes the treatment of Zcash.
items.dateNote: Retain the 2025 date visibly; this is background context, not a new October 2026 event.

freshnessCautions.note: BCB Resolution 589 of 23 September 2026 amended Article 91 of Resolution 520. The relevant restriction date is now 6 November 2026, not the original 30 October; the Article 91 amendment took effect 1 October. Other 589 provisions take effect 1 January 2027. Read current amendments before reusing original 520 text.

editorialRules: Keep publication, instrument/adoption, entry into force and application dates separate.
Legal status cannot be reliably inferred from a news-feed title; retain a reviewed curated rule record alongside automated discovery.
State actor and activity scope. A provider restriction is not a blanket ban on owning Zcash or using privacy.
Mark proposals, recommendations and reports explicitly; do not display them as enacted obligations.
Preserve actual source dates and distinguish historical background from newly published developments.
Allow only canonical primary domains; sanitize feed HTML and never execute markup or scripts.
Cache and deduplicate feeds by stable ID/canonical URL. A short rolling feed cannot establish complete coverage.
No legal or investment advice; no unsupported country-by-country legal/illegal badges.
